sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Warren County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Warren County Clerk's Office, inside the Warren County Courthouse at 413 Second Street in Belvidere. The office takes every document that affects ownership or transfer of residential, commercial and industrial property in the county, in person, by mail or electronically.

  • Main office: 908-475-6211.
  • Records room: 908-475-6011.
  • Public records inquiries: 908-475-6220.
  • Fax: 908-475-6208.

Hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, and the clerk asks visitors to call ahead and book an appointment so staff can serve each person efficiently. If your closing is set for late afternoon, have the title company confirm the recording method in advance.

Recorded documents become public records. Anyone may copy or research them during normal business hours, which is how buyers, lenders and title searchers confirm who owns a parcel and what liens or mortgages are attached. A certified copy costs $5 and ordinary copies are $2 a page, with a print from the clerk's website at five cents a page.

Warren County sits in northwestern New Jersey along the Delaware River, across from Easton, Pennsylvania. Belvidere is the county seat and Phillipsburg, with 15,249 residents in 2020, is the largest of its 22 municipalities. The 2025 estimate for the county is 112,953 residents. Hackettstown has the county's only NJ Transit rail stop.

A typical home value of $346,500 sits just under the $350,000 line the state uses to set its Realty Transfer Fee rates, so many local sales fall close to that dividing line.

A deed costs $40 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, plus a $10 tax abstract that applies to some documents such as deeds, court orders and easements. Selected charges from the clerk's State of New Jersey fee schedule:

The county charges nothing toward the homeless fund, and a veteran's DD-214 filing is free. A deed that runs past one page adds $10 for each extra sheet, so ask your title company to count pages before you budget the recording cost.

This form lets the clerk index the land record. Paper recordings without it carry a $20 indexing charge instead of the $10 fee. All land recordings filed on paper, and electronically recorded deeds, must include it. For documents sent through e-file, the page is required for deeds only.

Your title company or attorney normally prepares it with the deed. If you are handling a family transfer yourself, download the form from the clerk's website and attach it to the first sheet. A missing page is an avoidable surcharge and a possible delay.

The New Jersey Realty Transfer Fee is collected on top of the clerk's recording charges. The state sets it by the consideration stated in the deed. Ask your closing attorney for the exact figure, especially if you may qualify for the senior citizen partial exemption.

  • An Affidavit of Consideration (RTF-1) must be filed with any deed that claims a full or partial exemption.
  • The state lists 16 reasons for a full exemption, and partial exemptions exist for seniors, blind or disabled owners, low and moderate income housing and new construction.
  • A deed recorded in the wrong county must be re-recorded in the county where the land sits, with a refund application to the State on Form RTF-3.

Send the deed to Belvidere only when the land lies in Warren County.

sections.h2: How to search Warren County land records
sections.html:
Use the clerk's online public land records search. Choose the guest option and run a search by name to see every recorded document linked to that person, or narrow it to a specific instrument. Major subdivision maps are searchable by municipality, and a full-size map print costs $9 a sheet.

The Computer Access service in the clerk's vault lets visitors look up mortgages, deeds, liens, trade names, inheritance tax waivers, building contracts and maps on terminals. Law firms and title agents that record often can open a charge account with the clerk for recording, certified copies and map copies. Those charge accounts are separate from the accounts set up with the website vendor, which exist only to print copies from the site.

The clerk's office also handles notary oaths, trade names and certificates for documents going out of state, so a seller who needs a clerk's certificate can arrange it at the same visit, at $5 per certificate.

sections.h2: What to bring when you sell
sections.html:
Most sellers never visit the clerk, because the attorney or title company files the deed. If you do record on your own, bring the signed and acknowledged deed with the tax block and lot, the Data Recording Page, the Affidavit of Consideration if an exemption applies, and payment for the first-page and additional-page charges. Call 908-475-6211 first to book the appointment the clerk asks for.

After recording, a certified copy gives you proof of what was filed. A cash buyer purchasing as is uses the same office and the same fees, so a fast closing does not change the recording steps.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Warren County Clerk's Office?
faqs.a: 413 Second Street, Belvidere, NJ 07823, in the Warren County Courthouse. The main number is 908-475-6211, and the office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Call ahead for an appointment.

faqs.q: What will a Warren County deed filing set me back?
faqs.a: The deed charge is $40 for the first page and $10 for each added page, with a $10 tax abstract on some documents. Add the state Realty Transfer Fee, which depends on the stated consideration.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Warren County?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk records documents in person, by mail or electronically. For e-filed documents the Data Recording Page is required for deeds only.

faqs.q: What happens if I leave out the Data Recording Page?
faqs.a: Paper documents without it are charged $20 for indexing, against $10 when the page is attached. Electronically recorded deeds also need the page or the same charge applies.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for filing a veteran's discharge in Warren County?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists the DD-214 filing as no charge, along with a veteran's ID card and a peddler's license.
